themes.title: General-purpose humanoids
themes.description: Unitree's post-IPO crash is now confirmed as a two-week slide: Bloomberg's Sep 2 report has shares down ~50% from their Aug 19 intraday peak, a "fast reversal" that has hardened bubble warnings (Chatham House, BIS) rather than settling them. On the demand side, BMW's next-gen Figure 03 has replaced the retired Figure 02 at Spartanburg (which built 30,000+ X3s) and BMW is now piloting humanoids at its Leipzig, Germany plant too — real, if narrow, proof of deployed autonomy. Tesla's Optimus remains unverified — Musk's July shareholder letter still describes Fremont lines "being installed" with output "anticipated later this year."

themes.title: Warehouse & logistics automation
themes.description: Symbotic's story remains constructive: shares held near $42.81 (Sep 6, ~$26B market cap) after Q3 FY26 revenue hit $721M (+22% YoY) with GAAP profitability reached and backlog near $22.5-22.7B — a real improvement from the prior Goldman price-target cut and CTO share sale, though Barclays' Sell rating and the recent dilutive offering haven't gone away.

themes.title: Surgical robotics
themes.description: Intuitive Surgical traded near $366 (Sep 6), still down roughly a third YTD and on pace for its weakest year since 2008 — but Oppenheimer upgraded the stock to Outperform this week with a $500 target (24%+ implied upside), and the broader analyst consensus target ($508.68) points the same way. J&J's Ottava added a fresh data point: its bariatric-surgery pivotal study met endpoints at the ASMBS meeting, building on its July FDA de novo authorization. Medtronic's Hugo remains live in 30+ countries on its urology clearance.

themes.title: Defense autonomy & drones
themes.description: AeroVironment's $464.8M US Army LOCUST X3 laser-system award (Sep 3) sent shares up ~6%, but AVAV is still down roughly 40% YTD heading into its Sep 9 earnings report. Kratos picked up a new $20M+ contract from an Asian defense customer for mobile satcom gateways (Sep 1) and carries a $2.08B backlog, yet KTOS is still down 37% YTD. Contract wins and share prices remain decoupled in this sub-sector.

themes.title: Field robotics
themes.description: Caterpillar's new partnership with FieldAI (Sep 2) — its first concrete physical-AI tie-up this year — pairs Cat's jobsite data and engineering expertise with FieldAI's robot-agnostic foundation models for autonomous inspections, digital twins and situational awareness. Deere's autonomous articulated dump truck and commercial mowers continue routine operation. Both remain diversified industrials where robotics is a small slice of the overall return.

themes.title: Japanese factory automation
themes.description: Fanuc has slipped further, trading near ¥5,725 (Sep 2) versus ¥6,063 the prior week — confirmation the recovery from the Aug 3 guidance shock has stalled rather than resumed, even against a ¥7,351 average target; shares go ex-dividend Sep 29. Yaskawa has pulled back to the ¥4,500 area (Sep 3) after last week's rally. Keyence remains the outlier, trading near record highs in the ¥70,000-72,600 range.

themes.title: Supply chain & components
themes.description: MP Materials rallied to $54.53 (Sep 5) after Q2 revenue of $108.49M beat estimates by 13% on a 127% surge in NdPr sales volumes and adjusted EBITDA swung $41M higher YoY — then jumped further Sep 4 on reports Chinese producers are pausing US rare-earth shipments, with William Blair adding MP to its September Conviction List. Vishay Precision Group remains 2026's best-performing robotics supply-chain stock on booked humanoid-actuator orders.

themes.title: The robot "brain"
themes.description: NVIDIA's Jetson Thor platform (Blackwell-powered, 7.5x the AI compute of Jetson Orin) reached general availability in August, and the company unveiled new Blackwell-powered T3000/T2000 modules this week aimed at pushing mass-market robotics and edge AI further downmarket. Analog Devices became the latest Jetson Thor adopter (Sep 3), joining Agility, Amazon Robotics, Boston Dynamics, Caterpillar, Figure, Hexagon, Medtronic and Meta on a platform now used by 2M+ developers. The Aug 26 Q2 FY27 report (revenue $96.22B, Data Center $89B, Q3 guide $108B) still shows the compute layer dominating the sector's growth.

themes.title: China scaling & listing
themes.description: Unitree's extended slump is compounded by the FCC's new ban on foreign-made humanoid/quadruped robot imports, a direct regulatory headwind given China's ~85% share of the global humanoid market. LimX Dynamics closed a $200M pre-IPO round (valuing it at $2.2B / RMB 15B) and is preparing a Hong Kong listing; Agibot continues scaling shipments. Chinese humanoid startups are increasingly racing toward IPOs partly to open funding channels the FCC action and US investment curbs have narrowed.

bear_case.title: Unitree's crash is the bubble case made real
bear_case.description: Bloomberg reported Sep 2 that shares are now down ~50% from their Aug 19 intraday peak, a "fast reversal" now in its second straight week. Chatham House published a piece this month asking outright whether China's humanoid industry is a bubble, and the BIS has separately flagged that AI-linked asset valuations look overextended. This is no longer a hypothetical bubble warning — it's a live repricing investors can watch happen, now compounded by the FCC's new ban on foreign humanoid imports.

bear_case.title: Humanoid funding still outruns humanoid revenue
bear_case.description: Dealroom puts 2026 robotics funding near $55.8B — nearly double last year's record — while the median disclosed humanoid round remains in the hundreds of millions with rounds above $50M now the overwhelming majority of capital raised. Most of these companies still don't have revenue that justifies the price tag; one widely cited bear case on Figure AI specifically flags its valuation against Goldman's 2035 humanoid TAM estimate and an ongoing whistleblower lawsuit over safety allegations — notably in tension with BMW's own announcement this year expanding Figure deployments to a second plant in Leipzig, a discrepancy worth watching for clarification.

bear_case.title: Demos ≠ autonomy
bear_case.description: If a humanoid demo isn't explicitly labeled autonomous, assume teleoperation. Dexterity, inference speed, reliability, and cost still confine real use to structured factory/warehouse tasks.

bear_case.title: Crowding & shakeout risk
bear_case.description: 150+ companies chasing humanoids, with Agibot alone now claiming 15,000 cumulative units shipped; a reshuffling of startups is widely expected. Robotics pioneer Rodney Brooks argues much of the investment will be wasted.

bear_case.title: Backlogs and beats don't protect the stock
bear_case.description: Symbotic got a fresh Goldman price-target cut (to $45 from $54) and an insider share sale on top of a dilutive offering, despite real revenue growth and this quarter's GAAP profitability. AeroVironment and Kratos both won new contracts this month, yet their shares have traded down in 2026 anyway. In parts of this sector, balance-sheet and sentiment signals are doing more work than headline numbers.

bear_case.title: Revenue is elsewhere
bear_case.description: Industrial, logistics, and surgical robots generate proven revenue today; humanoids largely don't yet. Component and warehouse names carry less thesis risk than humanoid pure-plays.

bear_case.title: China price war
bear_case.description: Unitree's $5,900 R1 signals aggressive price compression that could squeeze Western OEM margins before the market matures — and 150+ Chinese humanoid startups, now including BYD, are competing on price and scale even as Unitree's own stock struggles to hold its valuation.

bear_case.title: "Dot-com stage" warnings
bear_case.description: KB Securities likened 2026's robotics/space enthusiasm to the final stage of the dot-com bubble; Ray Dalio separately compared the broader AI bubble to 1929 and 2000 valuation extremes. Sector EV/EBITDA multiples ranged from 0.9x (mature industrials) to 78.2x (speculative pure-plays) in Q4 2025 — a valuation split investors should not treat as one trade.

positions.note: Reached GAAP profitability this quarter on $721M revenue (+22% YoY) with backlog growing to ~$22.5-22.7B, and shares have held the $42-43 range — enough of a fundamental inflection to size a small position. Upgraded from Watch, though Barclays' Sell rating and the recent dilutive offering keep it capped rather than a full Core add.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.note: Oppenheimer upgraded to Outperform this week with a $500 target and J&J's Ottava cleared a bariatric-surgery pivotal endpoint at ASMBS — real positives, but shares are still down ~34% YTD on pace for the weakest year since 2008, so the valuation call still argues for waiting.

positions.name: Cognex
positions.note: No fresh catalyst since the HSBC downgrade to Hold ($65 PT); the underlying machine-vision business looks intact but nothing has emerged to justify moving off the sidelines.

positions.name: Caterpillar
positions.note: The new FieldAI partnership (Sep 2) is Caterpillar's first concrete physical-AI tie-up this year, but robotics remains a rounding error next to the construction-cycle exposure you'd actually be buying.

positions.name: Fanuc
positions.note: Shares slipped further to ¥5,725 (Sep 2) from ¥6,063 the week before — the recovery from the Aug 3 guidance shock now looks stalled rather than resumed.

positions.name: ABB Ltd
positions.note: Still awaiting regulatory clearance on the SoftBank robotics sale, with the division president set to depart by year-end — little left here to hold for ahead of a mid-to-late-2026 close.

positions.name: Serve Robotics
positions.note: Q2 missed on both lines and FY26 guidance was cut again to $9-10M; +404% YoY revenue growth still isn't outrunning the guidance cuts.

positions.name: Unitree
positions.note: Now down ~50% from its Aug 19 peak for a second straight week, and the FCC's new ban on foreign-made humanoid/quadruped imports closes off the US market entirely — moved from Watch to Avoid as both price action and policy have turned against it.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: RPA is being disrupted by the same AI agents it claims to ride, and the robotics label is marketing rather than hardware.
